football.label: American Football
football.why: Repeated collision and short sprints — force production and mass, with the posterior chain and trunk bracing carrying it.

soccer.label: Soccer
soccer.why: Repeated sprints over 90 minutes. Hamstring and groin work is the priority — they are the sport's two most common injuries.

basketball.label: Basketball
basketball.why: Jumping and decelerating. Landing mechanics and calf-to-knee tissue tolerance take precedence over top-end strength.

baseball.label: Baseball
baseball.why: Rotational velocity off one leg. Cuff and scapular work is protective, not optional, and trunk rotation is the transfer.

softball.label: Softball
softball.why: As baseball — rotational power with the shoulder complex kept resilient under a heavy throwing load.

volleyball.label: Volleyball
volleyball.why: Repeated jumping and overhead hitting. Jump capacity plus shoulder tolerance for a very high overhead volume.

swimming.label: Swimming
swimming.why: Enormous overhead volume with little ground contact. Scapular and cuff strength protect the shoulder; the trunk holds the line.

tennis.label: Tennis
tennis.why: Rotational and overhead under repeated change of direction. Shoulder, trunk and single-leg control together.

track.label: Track & Field
track.why: Rate of force development. Heavy compound work paired with jumps, kept well short of fatigue.

wrestling.label: Wrestling
wrestling.why: Strength at awkward angles under continuous fatigue. Grip, trunk and posterior chain, with hard conditioning.

lacrosse.label: Lacrosse
lacrosse.why: Sprinting and cutting with a rotational throw. Posterior chain and trunk, plus repeat-sprint conditioning.

golf.label: Golf
golf.why: One rotational effort repeated precisely. Hip mobility and trunk control protect the low back, which is golf's injury.

surfing.label: Surfing
surfing.why: Paddling endurance, an explosive pop-up, and constant trunk correction on an unstable base.

cycling.label: Cycling
cycling.why: Sustained one-legged force with no impact. Lifting exists to raise the ceiling and protect a rounded posture.

hockey.label: Ice Hockey
hockey.why: Skating is lateral hip extension. Adductor and glute work protect the groin, which is hockey's most common injury.

fieldhockey.label: Field Hockey
fieldhockey.why: Repeated sprints in a flexed posture. Posterior chain and trunk extension to offset the stick position.

gymnastics.label: Gymnastics
gymnastics.why: Relative strength and control through extreme range. Bodyweight mastery before external load.

boxing.label: Boxing
boxing.why: Rotational punching power over rounds. Trunk rotation, shoulder endurance and legs that keep moving.

mma.label: MMA
mma.why: Every quality at once under fatigue. Strength held, power expressed, conditioning across all three energy systems.

martialarts.label: Martial Arts
martialarts.why: Explosive striking and kicking from a stable base, with the hip mobility the kicks require.

waterpolo.label: Water Polo
waterpolo.why: Throwing and wrestling while treading. Shoulder durability under a very high overhead volume.

xc.label: Cross Country
xc.why: Aerobic capacity first. Lifting is low-volume and heavy to improve economy and tolerate mileage.

beachvb.label: Beach Volleyball
beachvb.why: Jumping from sand doubles the demand on the calf and hip; overhead volume stays high.

badminton.label: Badminton
badminton.why: Repeated lunging and overhead reach. Ankle and knee deceleration with shoulder tolerance.

pickleball.label: Pickleball
pickleball.why: Short lateral movement and quick stops. Knee and hip control matter more than top-end output.

cheer.label: Cheerleading
cheer.why: Overhead stabilising under load, tumbling power, and landings that must be controlled every time.

diving.label: Diving
diving.why: Explosive take-off with total trunk control in the air, and shoulders that tolerate entry.

rowing.label: Rowing
rowing.why: Repeated maximal leg drive through the trunk. Low back and posterior chain are the priority and the risk.

skateboarding.label: Skateboarding
skateboarding.why: Repeated impact absorption on one leg with ankle and knee tolerance for awkward landings.

snowboarding.label: Snowboarding
snowboarding.why: Sustained isometric leg strength with rotational control and hard eccentric landings.

skiing.label: Alpine Skiing
skiing.why: Long eccentric and isometric quad work. Knee integrity is the whole game — the ACL is the sport's injury.

rugby.label: Rugby
rugby.why: Collision plus 80 minutes of running. Mass and strength held under a heavy aerobic load.

ultimate.label: Ultimate Frisbee
ultimate.why: Repeated sprints, cuts and layouts. Hamstring and knee resilience with real aerobic depth.

triathlon.label: Triathlon
triathlon.why: Three aerobic disciplines. Lifting is minimal, heavy and infrequent — enough to hold tissue, never enough to interfere.

weightlifting.label: Weightlifting
weightlifting.why: Maximal strength expressed at speed overhead. Squat and pull strength with overhead position tolerance.

powerlifting.label: Powerlifting
powerlifting.why: Three lifts, maximal load. Everything else exists to support squat, bench and deadlift.

crossfit.label: CrossFit
crossfit.why: Broad capacity across every quality. Strength kept honest while conditioning stays high.

fencing.label: Fencing
fencing.why: Explosive single-leg lunging repeated for hours, with the trailing hip taking an unusual load.

archery.label: Archery
archery.why: Sustained isometric draw. Scapular endurance and postural strength, both sides trained evenly.

bowling.label: Bowling
bowling.why: A one-sided repeated swing and slide. Trunk control and hip stability keep the low back out of it.

equestrian.label: Equestrian
equestrian.why: Continuous trunk and hip stabilising in a flexed position, with adductor endurance.

figureskating.label: Figure Skating
figureskating.why: Single-leg jump take-off and landing, rotational control, and a high hip mobility requirement.

trackcycling.label: Track Cycling
trackcycling.why: Short maximal efforts. Squat and hip-extension strength translate closely to standing-start power.

bmx.label: BMX
bmx.why: A maximal standing start plus repeated impact absorption through arms and legs.

climbing.label: Rock Climbing
climbing.why: Relative pulling strength and grip endurance. Pressing and lower-body work balance a very pull-dominant sport.

flagfootball.label: Flag Football
flagfootball.why: Sprinting and cutting without collision. Hamstring resilience and repeat-sprint capacity.

handball.label: Handball
handball.why: Jumping and overhead throwing with contact. Shoulder durability alongside lower-body power.

kickboxing.label: Kickboxing
kickboxing.why: Striking with the legs and hands over rounds. Rotational power, hip mobility and conditioning.

muaythai.label: Muay Thai
muaythai.why: Clinch strength and repeated kicking. Trunk, hip and calf tissue tolerance under heavy volume.

judo.label: Judo
judo.why: Gripping and throwing from awkward positions. Pulling strength, grip and trunk above all.

bjj.label: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu
bjj.why: Isometric strength under fatigue with a large hip mobility requirement. Neck and grip need care.
